title: Normal form for a nonnegative one-bit function
statement: Let $f\colon\{0,1\}^1\to\mathbb R$ be nonnegative at every point and not identically zero. Then there exist real numbers $c$ and $a$ such that $c>0$, $-1\le a\le1$, and $f(x)=c\bigl(1+a\sigma(x_0)\bigr)$ for every $x\in\{0,1\}^1$, where $\sigma(0)=1$ and $\sigma(1)=-1$.
replaced: For every nonnegative function $f:\{0,1\}\to[0,\infty)$ that is not identically zero, there exist $c>0$ and $a\in[-1,1]$ such that $f(t)=c(1+a(-1)^t)$ for both bits $t$.
